title: Timestamps are London local time with a literal Z appended — BST values are an hour wrong

oracle.activityBoundary: every callActivity argument and return value crosses oracle/lib/boundary.js
oracle.determinismCheck: the case was run twice at clockPinIso and the two document arrays compared

edits: no edits at all. This is base__prosecution-case re-recorded under pinning/ so the D9 assertion has a case of its own that a future edit to the corpus cannot quietly move.

digests.convention: sha256 of the written file bytes — `sha256sum <file>` reproduces each value exactly

nodeEvidence.what: getLocalDateTime: `moment_timeZone.tz(dateString, "Europe/London").format('YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ss') + 'Z'` — the value is converted INTO London local time and then given a UTC designator. During BST the printed instant is one hour later than the instant it claims to be.
formatDateAndGetLocalDateTime — durationStartDate / durationEndDate — appends the same literal Z.
populateFileName uses getLocalDate (DateService.js:29, 'YYYY-MM-DD' London local), so around midnight the filename date and the registerDate date can disagree with UTC.

assertion: The input is the prosecution-case fixture with sharedTime "2020-06-01T10:00:00Z" — 1 June, British Summer Time, 11:00 in London. Assert EXACTLY, on both documents: registerDate equals the STRING "2020-06-01T11:00:00Z", and fileName equals "InformantRegister_TFL_2020-06-01.csv" / "InformantRegister_TVL_2020-06-01.csv". Assert on the exact string. Do NOT parse it into an Instant/OffsetDateTime and compare instants — that comparison passes for both the right answer and the wrong one and pins nothing. THE CONTROL: recorded/base__outbound-hearing has sharedTime "2020-01-20T11:00:00Z" (GMT) and registerDate "2020-01-20T11:00:00Z" — unchanged, because London is UTC in January. The pair proves the +1h is a BST artefact, not a constant. A java.time port that does the honest thing — sharedTime.atZone(ZoneId.of("Europe/London")).toOffsetDateTime() rendered as "2020-06-01T11:00:00+01:00", or the instant re-rendered as "2020-06-01T10:00:00Z" — is CORRECT and MUST STILL FAIL this test. D9 is priority-2: prosecuting authorities parse these values out of the CSV (design doc §13 Q9), so the correction cannot ship before that check and a DEVIATIONS.md entry. This test is the tripwire that makes an unauthorised correction visible in CI on the day it is written.
